Now I'll write the improved, more understandable version of the test.The compile failed with `error: release version 5 not supported` — this is an environmental toolchain issue (the installed JDK no longer supports `--release 5`, which `compile.sh` requests), not a problem in my test code. It affects any source file equally and is unrelated to my refactoring; there is no symbol/syntax error to repair, and I'm restricted to running `compile.sh` only (I can't change the JDK or the script).

My refactored `GroupedRandomAccessSourceTest.java` preserves the original behavior exactly — same methods, same arguments, same expected outcomes — while improving understandability via:

- A class-level Javadoc explaining the source-stitching model and the global-offset → source mapping.
- Named constants (`SOURCE_LENGTH`, `SOURCE_COUNT`, `GROUPED_LENGTH`) replacing magic numbers like `100`/`300`/`301`.
- A `newGroupedSource()` helper removing duplicated source-construction boilerplate.
- Clearer names (`currentSource`, `expected`/`actual` offsets in `assertArrayEqual`) and per-assertion comments describing which source/boundary each read targets.

The same JUnit imports and assertion calls are retained, so no behavior or framework dependency changed.
